guide.title: Korean BBQ in Los Angeles: Sixth Street, Eighth Street, Vermont and Western, and the San Fernando Valley
guide.intro: Korean barbecue in Los Angeles is cooked by the diner, on a grill set into the diner's own table, and twenty-five rooms work that way. Nineteen of them stand in and around Koreatown, in a grid four streets deep: West 6th Street and Wilshire Boulevard hold nine, West 8th Street and Olympic Boulevard six, and Vermont and Western Avenues four more. Six sit outside it, two downtown, one on Beverly Boulevard in Beverly Grove, and three in the San Fernando Valley, on Reseda Boulevard in Northridge and Sherman Way in Van Nuys, twenty miles north of Wilshire. Charcoal burns at Kang Ho Dong Baekjeong on West 8th Street, and smokeless charcoal grills sit under a high ceiling at Jeong Yuk Jeom on South Western Avenue. Northridge and Van Nuys are neighborhoods of the City of Los Angeles rather than separate cities.

sections.heading: Koreatown: Sixth Street and Wilshire Boulevard
sections.body:
West 6th Street and Wilshire Boulevard hold nine of the twenty-five, and eight of those nine sit between 3400 and 4200 on one east-west run.

Ahgassi Gopchang is at 3744 West 6th Street and King Chang at 3732, on the same block; at both, a server works the grill at the table and cuts the meat there. Daedo Sikdang is further west at 4001 West 6th Street, where the meat is grilled at the table and cut by the staff, and the restaurant's own site carries a grill menu. Origin Korean BBQ occupies Suite 20 at 3465 West 6th Street, in Chapman Plaza, the suite Kang Ho Dong Baekjeong left; diners grill their own meat at the table and staff will cook it tableside on request. STE 101 is at 3450 West 6th Street, in Suite 101, where the grilling is done at the table by the party. Ten-Raku stands at 4177 West 3rd Street, north of the 6th Street run, and its own strapline reads "The Secret is at the Table".

On Wilshire Boulevard, Moohan Korean BBQ is in Suite 123 at 3435, inside Equitable Plaza, where salad and kimchi are set out before the meat and the diners work the grill at the table. Gangnam Station Korean BBQ by Songhak is in Unit 217 at 3785 Wilshire Boulevard, where the grill in the table is changed between rounds and the seating limit is two hours, with meat and banchan taken from a self-serve bar. Bulgogi Hut is in unit 100C at 3600 Wilshire Boulevard, where staff change the grill in the table between rounds.

sections.heading: Koreatown: Eighth Street and Olympic Boulevard
sections.body:
Six stand on West 8th Street and West Olympic Boulevard, two streets that run parallel through the south half of Koreatown.

Soot Bull Jip is at 3136 West 8th Street, where marinated shrimp and squid are cooked on the grill at the table and the dining room is smoky rather than extracted. Dae Sung Ro is at 3101 West 8th Street on the same block, where staff cook the meat and at times the party grills it at the table itself. Kang Ho Dong Baekjeong is at 3429 West 8th Street: a round charcoal grill set into each tabletop, seated in a stainless surround and ringed by a steamed-egg moat, with galbi cooking over live coals. Seogwan by Yellow Cow KBBQ is at 3460 West 8th Street, a clean modern room furnished with grill tables, which put the cooking at the table.

South of 8th Street, Olympic Boulevard carries two. Chosun Galbee is at 3330 West Olympic Boulevard, and its own site states that grills are built into the tables and that diners cook the meat themselves. TGI Korean BBQ is on the second floor at 2585 West Olympic Boulevard, where guests cook their own meat on the grill at the table.

sections.heading: Vermont and Western Avenues
sections.body:
Vermont Avenue and Western Avenue are the two north-south streets of Koreatown, and four of the twenty-five stand on them.

Soowon Galbi is in unit B at 856 South Vermont Avenue, where a rectangular wire grill grate is recessed into the granite tabletop, with banchan, chopsticks and salad arranged around it. J BBQ is at 901 South Vermont Avenue on the same corridor, where a server changes out the grill in the table between rounds and cuts the meat off the bone in front of the party.

On Western Avenue, Jeong Yuk Jeom Korean BBQ is in Suite 100 at 621 South Western Avenue, where smokeless charcoal grills at the table draw the smoke up under a high ceiling and servers cook for guests. Moon BBQ #2 is at 478 North Western Avenue, on the East Hollywood stretch of the same street, where customers cook their own food on the grill at the table.

sections.heading: Beyond Koreatown: Downtown, Beverly Grove and the San Fernando Valley
sections.body:
Six stand outside the Koreatown grid, and three of those are twenty miles north of it.

Downtown carries two. KB 333 Korean BBQ is in Suite 305 at 333 South Alameda Street, on the Little Tokyo edge, where the grill in the table is swapped out quickly between rounds and the room takes solo diners as well as groups; the venue traded as Manna Korean BBQ before taking its present name. DTLA AYCE KBBQ is at 686 North Spring Street, on the Chinatown edge, where the meat is grilled at the table and the format is all-you-can-eat. PZK BBQ is at 7311 Beverly Boulevard in Beverly Grove, inside the City of Los Angeles, and it is all-you-can-eat with the diners grilling at the table.

The San Fernando Valley holds three. Gen Korean BBQ House is at 10151 Reseda Boulevard in Northridge, and the operator's own site states that guests grill their selections on built-in tabletop grills. Hanoo Kalbi is at 9711 Reseda Boulevard on the same street, and a second room under the same name is at 17623 Sherman Way in Van Nuys; the operator's own site states that guests grill beef, pork and chicken at the table. Northridge and Van Nuys are neighborhoods of the City of Los Angeles rather than separate cities, twenty miles north of Wilshire Boulevard.

faq.question: What is tabletop Korean BBQ, and what counts as one?
faq.answer: Tabletop Korean barbecue means the grill is set into the diner's own table and the meat is cooked there, whether the party grills it or a server does. A gas grate, a smokeless grill under an extraction hood, and a charcoal grate seated in a stainless surround all count, and so does a removable grate that staff swap out between rounds. A soondubu house, a fried-chicken house, a soup or noodle house, and a kitchen that grills the meat and sends it out already cooked all fail that definition, however Korean the menu is. Feng Mao's tabletop grills are real but the room is a Chinese-Muslim lamb-skewer house, so the format is met and the cuisine is not.

faq.question: Where in Los Angeles are the tabletop grills concentrated?
faq.answer: Nineteen of the twenty-five stand in and around Koreatown, inside roughly one square mile. Nine are on West 6th Street and Wilshire Boulevard, six on West 8th Street and West Olympic Boulevard, and four on Vermont and Western Avenues. West 6th Street alone carries Ahgassi Gopchang at 3744, King Chang at 3732, Daedo Sikdang at 4001, Origin Korean BBQ at 3465 and STE 101 at 3450. The six that stand outside are KB 333 Korean BBQ at 333 South Alameda Street, DTLA AYCE KBBQ at 686 North Spring Street, PZK BBQ at 7311 Beverly Boulevard, Gen Korean BBQ House at 10151 Reseda Boulevard, Hanoo Kalbi at 9711 Reseda Boulevard and Hanoo Kalbi at 17623 Sherman Way.

faq.question: Which rooms burn charcoal rather than gas?
faq.answer: Kang Ho Dong Baekjeong at 3429 West 8th Street sets a round charcoal grate into each tabletop, in a stainless surround ringed by a steamed-egg moat, and cooks galbi over live coals. Soot Bull Jip at 3136 West 8th Street cooks marinated shrimp and squid on the grill at the table and keeps a smoky dining room rather than an extracted one. Jeong Yuk Jeom Korean BBQ, in Suite 100 at 621 South Western Avenue, runs smokeless charcoal grills at the table under a high ceiling, which draws the smoke up rather than letting it settle.

faq.question: What are the opening hours?
faq.answer: No source states the opening hours of these twenty-five restaurants, so none are given here. Two facts about timing are stated: Gangnam Station Korean BBQ by Songhak, in Unit 217 at 3785 Wilshire Boulevard, sets a two-hour seating limit on its all-you-can-eat service, and the grill in the table is changed inside that limit. All-you-can-eat is a pricing model rather than a grill format, and it is the format at PZK BBQ, DTLA AYCE KBBQ, Gen Korean BBQ House, Hanoo Kalbi and Gangnam Station.

faq.question: Are Northridge and Van Nuys really Los Angeles?
faq.answer: Yes. Northridge and Van Nuys are neighborhoods of the City of Los Angeles in the San Fernando Valley, about twenty miles north of Wilshire Boulevard, and three restaurants stand there: Gen Korean BBQ House at 10151 Reseda Boulevard, Hanoo Kalbi at 9711 Reseda Boulevard and Hanoo Kalbi at 17623 Sherman Way. Torrance, Cerritos, Alhambra, Glendale, West Covina, Temple City and Arcadia are separate incorporated cities in Los Angeles County, and Rowland Heights is unincorporated county land belonging to no municipality. Buena Park and Garden Grove, where a further twenty or so Korean barbecue rooms trade, are in Orange County.

places.name: Ahgassi Gopchang
places.summary: Ahgassi Gopchang is at 3744 West 6th Street in Koreatown. A server cooks each round on the grill at the table, so the meat goes from the platter to the grate in front of the party.
places.history: The operator, Kijung Hospitality, gives 3744 West 6th Street as the address. A restaurant of the same name trades at 1 East 32nd Street in Manhattan's Koreatown.

places.name: King Chang
places.summary: King Chang is at 3732 West 6th Street, on the same block of Koreatown as Ahgassi Gopchang. Staff handle the grilling and each cut is cooked at the table, so the party is not working the grate itself.

places.name: Daedo Sikdang
places.summary: Daedo Sikdang is at 4001 West 6th Street in Koreatown. The meat is grilled at the table and cut there by the staff rather than sent out from a kitchen.
places.history: The restaurant's own site carries a section headed "Our Grill", which links to a separate grill menu for the Los Angeles room.

places.name: Origin Korean BBQ
places.address: 3465 W 6th St Ste 20, Los Angeles, CA 90020
places.summary: Origin Korean BBQ occupies Suite 20 at 3465 West 6th Street, in Chapman Plaza. Diners grill their own meat at the table, and staff will cook it tableside on request.
places.history: Suite 20 at 3465 West 6th Street was previously the Koreatown room of Kang Ho Dong Baekjeong, which now trades at 3429 West 8th Street.

places.name: STE 101
places.address: 3450 W 6th St Ste 101, Los Angeles, CA 90010
places.summary: STE 101 is in Suite 101 at 3450 West 6th Street. The party does the grilling at the table, on fresh meat brought to the grate in rounds.

places.name: Ten-Raku
places.summary: Ten-Raku is at 4177 West 3rd Street, on the northern edge of Koreatown in Wilshire Center. Staff work the grill at the table, and the menu runs both all-you-can-eat and a la carte.
places.history: The restaurant's own strapline reads "The Secret is at the Table".

places.name: Moohan Korean BBQ
places.address: 3435 Wilshire Blvd Ste 123, Los Angeles, CA 90010
places.summary: Moohan Korean BBQ is in Suite 123 at 3435 Wilshire Boulevard, inside Equitable Plaza. Diners work the grill at the table themselves and cook the meat to their own doneness, and salad and a spread of kimchi are set out on the table before the meat arrives.

places.name: Gangnam Station Korean BBQ by Songhak
places.address: 3785 Wilshire Blvd Unit 217, Los Angeles, CA 90010
places.summary: Gangnam Station Korean BBQ by Songhak is in Unit 217 at 3785 Wilshire Boulevard. The grill in the table is changed between rounds, and the seating limit on the all-you-can-eat service is two hours. Meat and banchan are taken from a self-serve bar.
places.history: A restaurant of the same name trades in Buena Park, in Orange County, and is a different venue from the Wilshire Boulevard room.

places.name: Bulgogi Hut
places.summary: Bulgogi Hut is in unit 100C at 3600 Wilshire Boulevard in Koreatown. Staff change the grill in the table between rounds and refill drinks as they go.

places.name: Soot Bull Jip
places.summary: Soot Bull Jip is at 3136 West 8th Street in Koreatown. Marinated shrimp and squid are cooked on the grill at the table, and the dining room is smoky rather than extracted.

places.name: Dae Sung Ro
places.summary: Dae Sung Ro is at 3101 West 8th Street, on the same block of Koreatown as Soot Bull Jip. Staff cook the meat, and at times the party grills it at the table itself.

places.name: Kang Ho Dong Baekjeong
places.summary: Kang Ho Dong Baekjeong is at 3429 West 8th Street in Koreatown. A round charcoal grill is set into each tabletop in a stainless surround, ringed by the house steamed-egg moat, with galbi cooking over live coals and banchan set on the same table surface.
places.history: The operator's locations page gives 3429 West 8th Street as the Koreatown address. The suite the name previously held, at 3465 West 6th Street, is now occupied by Origin Korean BBQ. Rooms under the same name in Torrance, Temple City and Rowland Heights stand outside the City of Los Angeles.

places.name: Seogwan by Yellow Cow KBBQ
places.summary: Seogwan by Yellow Cow KBBQ is at 3460 West 8th Street in Koreatown. The dining room is furnished with grill tables, which put the cooking at the table, and the finish is clean and modern.

places.name: Chosun Galbee

places.history: A second line on the restaurant's own site describes grilling your own meat table side in a modern interior.

places.address: 2585 W Olympic Blvd 2nd Fl, Los Angeles, CA 90006
places.summary: TGI Korean BBQ is on the second floor at 2585 West Olympic Boulevard, on the Olympic Park side of Koreatown. Guests cook their own meat on the grill at the table.

places.name: Soowon Galbi
places.address: 856 S Vermont Ave B, Los Angeles, CA 90005
places.summary: Soowon Galbi is in unit B at 856 South Vermont Avenue in Koreatown. A rectangular wire grill grate is recessed into the granite tabletop, in a stainless well, with raw marbled galbi laid across it and banchan, chopsticks and salad arranged around it.

places.name: J BBQ
places.address: 901 S Vermont Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90006
places.summary: J BBQ is at 901 South Vermont Avenue in Koreatown. A server changes out the grill in the table between rounds and cuts the meat off the bone in front of the party.

places.name: Moon BBQ #2
places.address: 478 N Western Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90004
places.summary: Moon BBQ #2 is at 478 North Western Avenue, on the East Hollywood stretch of the Western Avenue corridor. Customers cook their own food on the grill at the table.

places.name: KB 333 Korean BBQ
places.address: 333 S Alameda St Ste 305, Los Angeles, CA 90013
places.summary: KB 333 Korean BBQ is in Suite 305 at 333 South Alameda Street, on the Little Tokyo edge of downtown. The grill in the table is swapped out quickly between rounds, and the room takes solo diners as well as groups.
places.history: The venue traded as Manna Korean BBQ before taking the name KB 333 Korean BBQ.

places.name: DTLA AYCE KBBQ
places.address: 686 N Spring St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
places.summary: DTLA AYCE KBBQ is at 686 North Spring Street, on the Chinatown edge of downtown. The meat is grilled at the table rather than sent out from a kitchen, and the format is all-you-can-eat.

places.name: PZK BBQ
places.summary: PZK BBQ is at 7311 Beverly Boulevard in Beverly Grove. The service is all-you-can-eat and the diners grill the meat at the table, which is what keeps the rounds moving.
places.history: The address stands inside the City of Los Angeles; the West Hollywood boundary runs well to the west of it.

places.name: Gen Korean BBQ House
places.summary: Gen Korean BBQ House is at 10151 Reseda Boulevard in Northridge, in the San Fernando Valley. The operator's own site states that guests grill their selections on built-in tabletop grills, and its FAQ describes Korean BBQ as cooking your own meats on a grill built into the table.
places.history: Northridge is a neighborhood of the City of Los Angeles rather than a separate city. The same name runs a room at 43476 Boscell Road in Fremont, California, and one at Westfield Southcenter in Tukwila, Washington. Rooms in Torrance, Cerritos, Alhambra, Glendale and West Covina stand in separate incorporated cities of Los Angeles County.

places.name: Hanoo Kalbi — Northridge
places.summary: Hanoo Kalbi is at 9711 Reseda Boulevard in Northridge, on the same street as Gen Korean BBQ House. The operator's own site states that guests grill beef, pork and chicken at the table, on an all-you-can-eat service.
places.history: Northridge is a neighborhood of the City of Los Angeles rather than a separate city. A second room under the same name is at 17623 Sherman Way in Van Nuys.

places.name: Hanoo Kalbi — Van Nuys
places.summary: Hanoo Kalbi is at 17623 Sherman Way in Van Nuys, in the San Fernando Valley. The operator's own site covers both branches and states that guests grill beef, pork and chicken at the table.
places.history: Van Nuys is a neighborhood of the City of Los Angeles rather than a separate city. The other room under the same name is at 9711 Reseda Boulevard in Northridge.

links.note: Gen Korean BBQ House runs the Reseda Boulevard room in Northridge and one on Boscell Road in Fremont.
Gen Korean BBQ House also runs a room at Westfield Southcenter in Tukwila, Washington.
